title: Vikas Gupta & Another v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
coram: Pankaj Mithal, J. & Pankaj Bhatia, J.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed on the ground of alternative remedy
headnote: Where a theft assessment has become final (the provisional assessments having been treated as final for want of objection) and the consumer's only grievance is that he was never served the notice, the disputed question of service of notice is more appropriately dealt with in an appeal under Section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 against the final assessment. If the consumer wishes to pay in instalments, he may move the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. In view of these alternative remedies, the writ was dismissed.

holding_units.topic: Disputed service of notice is for the s.127 appeal; instalments via Clause 6.14
holding_units.question: Should the writ court decide a disputed question of service of the assessment notice, or is that for the s.127 appeal?
holding_units.holding: The disputed question of service of notice depends on facts more appropriately dealt with in a s.127 appeal against the final assessments; and instalments, if desired, are for the Executive Engineer under Clause 6.14. Given these alternative remedies, the writ was dismissed with liberty to avail them.
holding_units.limiting_facts: Two checkings (7.9.2017, 19.1.2018) alleged theft; provisional assessments treated as final for want of objection; demand notices sent by registered post; consumer alleged non-service.

principle_tags.application: A disputed question of service of the assessment notice is for the s.127 appeal against the final assessment, not the writ court; instalments are for the Clause 6.14 Executive Engineer.

not_decided.point: Whether the assessment notices were served
not_decided.note: Disputed fact left to the s.127 appellate authority.
